inputs.proposal: J2534 request modes: the set scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs, ?poll= is rejected at parse time unless ?filter= gives it a channel, and the single-PID poll request is built on the first channel.

blockers: claim: Missing channel validation for poll mode: old code checked (sched_mode || params.poll_pid != 0) && chan_count == 0, new code only checks sched_mode && chan_count == 0; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: if (sched_mode && t->chan_count == 0) {
questions: What is the definition of rx_id in j2534_uri_params? Does it get set from profile-declared channels, making the parse_query filter check overly restrictive for profiles that declare their own channels?
What does channel_index_for_rx and rx_for_pid do? The removal of these lookups suggests poll PIDs may now use the wrong channel.
Is there a thread-safety analysis for the transport's shared state? The diff shows no mutex changes but modifies request mode logic.

claim: Out-of-bounds array access: new code uses t->chans[0] directly without validating chan_count > 0; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: build_mode01_request(req, t->chans[0].tx_id, t->poll_pid);
nits: The parse_query comment change from 'poll needs a channel to receive on, but the channel may come from the profile' to 'poll without filter is rejected' is a significant semantic change that breaks existing use cases.
Consider adding a NULL check for t->chans before the array access, even if chan_count > 0 is now checked elsewhere.
